source_meta._title: More than six banner patterns can be added to a banner

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2 in a single-player Creative-mode world. Use one local player, the normal player inventory, and a placed Loom. No seed, coordinates, commands, data packs, server, operator permissions, or special graphics settings are required by the report.
preconditions: Launch exactly Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2, the first version listed as affected; do not use fix version 22w18a.
Use an unmodified vanilla client so that mods do not alter the Loom interface or inventory behavior.
Create or enter a Creative-mode world where the player can place and interact with blocks.
Keep at least three player-inventory slots empty so the two banners and displaced dye can be moved without closing the Loom interface.
The instructions use the default inventory key E and right-click interaction; use the corresponding bound controls if they have been changed.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select and start the installation for Java Edition 1.15.2. Wait for the main menu to finish loading and confirm that the lower-left version label shows 1.15.2.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and displays version 1.15.2.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, create a new world in Creative Mode, and enter it. A default world type and arbitrary seed are sufficient. Wait until nearby terrain is rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a loaded Creative-mode world and can move normally.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Use the Search Items tab to obtain one Loom, two White Banners, a stack of Red Dye, and at least one Blue Dye. Put the Loom in the hotbar and keep the banners and dyes in accessible inventory slots. The colors are deterministic implementation choices; the report does not require particular colors.
steps.exact_input: Loom; White Banner; Red Dye; Blue Dye
steps.success_cue: The inventory contains one Loom, two plain White Banners, Red Dye, and Blue Dye.

steps.action: Close the inventory, select the Loom in the hotbar, aim at the top surface of a nearby solid block, and right-click to place the Loom.
steps.success_cue: A Loom block is placed within interaction range of the player.

steps.action: Aim at the placed Loom and right-click to open its interface. Identify the banner input slot and dye input slot on the left, the pattern-selection area in the middle, and the result/output slot on the right.
steps.success_cue: The Loom interface is open, including the player inventory at the bottom and the Loom output slot on the right.

steps.action: Move one of the plain White Banners from the player inventory into the Loom's banner input slot. Leave the other White Banner in the player inventory; that untouched item is the second banner used later.
steps.success_cue: One plain White Banner is in the Loom's banner input slot and another plain White Banner remains in the player inventory.

steps.action: Move the stack of Red Dye into the Loom's dye input slot. No separate Banner Pattern item is needed for the six simple geometric patterns used below.
steps.success_cue: The first White Banner and Red Dye are in their respective Loom input slots, and the ordinary pattern buttons are available.

steps.action: In the pattern-selection area, left-click the icon depicting a horizontal stripe along the top edge of the banner.
steps.success_cue: A result banner preview with the selected red top stripe is present in the right-hand output slot.

steps.action: Left-click the output slot once to take the patterned banner. Do not shift-click. The input banner and one Red Dye are consumed by this Loom operation.
steps.success_cue: The once-patterned banner is attached to the cursor, and the Loom's banner input slot is empty.

steps.action: Left-click the empty banner input slot to place the once-patterned banner back into the Loom.
steps.success_cue: The once-patterned banner is in the banner input slot and Red Dye remains in the dye slot.

steps.action: Left-click the pattern icon depicting a horizontal stripe along the bottom edge of the banner.
steps.success_cue: A new result preview is present in the output slot with the selected bottom stripe added after the first layer.

steps.action: Left-click the output slot once to take the modified banner.
steps.success_cue: The twice-patterned banner is attached to the cursor, and the Loom's banner input slot is empty.

steps.action: Place the twice-patterned banner back into the Loom's banner input slot.
steps.success_cue: The twice-patterned banner is in the banner input slot and the remaining Red Dye is still available.

steps.action: Left-click the pattern icon depicting a vertical stripe along the left edge of the banner.
steps.success_cue: A result preview with the selected left-edge stripe as the next layer is present in the output slot.

steps.action: Left-click the output slot once to take the modified banner.
steps.success_cue: The three-pattern banner is attached to the cursor, and the Loom's banner input slot is empty.

steps.action: Place the three-pattern banner back into the Loom's banner input slot.
steps.success_cue: The three-pattern banner is in the banner input slot and Red Dye remains in the dye slot.

steps.action: Left-click the pattern icon depicting a vertical stripe along the right edge of the banner.
steps.success_cue: A result preview with the selected right-edge stripe as the next layer is present in the output slot.

steps.action: Left-click the output slot once to take the modified banner.
steps.success_cue: The four-pattern banner is attached to the cursor, and the Loom's banner input slot is empty.

steps.action: Place the four-pattern banner back into the Loom's banner input slot.
steps.success_cue: The four-pattern banner is in the banner input slot and Red Dye remains in the dye slot.

steps.action: Left-click the pattern icon depicting a vertical stripe through the center of the banner.
steps.success_cue: A result preview with the selected center vertical stripe as the next layer is present in the output slot.

steps.action: Left-click the output slot once to take the modified banner.
steps.success_cue: The five-pattern banner is attached to the cursor, and the Loom's banner input slot is empty.

steps.action: Place the five-pattern banner back into the Loom's banner input slot.
steps.success_cue: The five-pattern banner is in the banner input slot and Red Dye remains in the dye slot.

steps.action: Left-click the pattern icon depicting a horizontal stripe through the center of the banner. This is the sixth pattern layer for the first banner.
steps.success_cue: A result preview with the center horizontal stripe as the sixth layer is present in the output slot.

steps.action: Left-click the output slot once to take the modified first banner. Do not place it back into the Loom yet.
steps.success_cue: The first banner is attached to the cursor after six normal Loom operations, and the banner input slot is empty.

steps.action: Place the first banner into a distinct empty slot in the player inventory. Hover over it and count the pattern-description lines in its tooltip, confirming that it has exactly six pattern layers. Remember this inventory slot because this banner must be swapped into the Loom later.
steps.success_cue: The six-pattern first banner is stored in a known player-inventory slot, while the separate plain second White Banner remains available.

steps.action: Replace the Red Dye in the Loom's dye slot with Blue Dye: pick up the remaining Red Dye, place it into an empty player-inventory slot, then pick up the Blue Dye and place it into the dye input slot.
steps.success_cue: Blue Dye is in the Loom's dye input slot, the Red Dye is outside the Loom, and the banner input slot is empty.

steps.action: Move the untouched second White Banner from the player inventory into the Loom's banner input slot.
steps.success_cue: The plain second White Banner is in the banner input slot, Blue Dye is in the dye slot, and the six-pattern first banner remains in the player inventory.

steps.action: In the Loom's pattern-selection area, left-click the icon depicting a centered circle. Leave the resulting second banner in the right-hand output slot: do not click, shift-click, or otherwise remove that output.
steps.success_cue: The centered-circle pattern remains selected and a blue-circle result for the second banner is waiting in the right-hand output slot.

steps.action: While the second banner's result remains untouched in the output slot, left-click the six-pattern first banner in the player inventory so that it becomes attached to the cursor.
steps.success_cue: The six-pattern first banner is attached to the cursor; the plain second banner is still in the Loom input slot and its selected result has not been taken.

steps.action: Left-click the occupied Loom banner input slot while holding the six-pattern first banner. This inventory click must directly swap the held first banner with the second banner already in the input slot; do not remove the right-hand output before making this swap.
steps.success_cue: The six-pattern first banner is now in the Loom's banner input slot, and the displaced plain second banner is attached to the cursor.

steps.action: Move the displaced second banner from the cursor into an empty player-inventory slot. Do not change the banner input, dye input, selected centered-circle pattern, or right-hand output slot.
steps.success_cue: The cursor is empty, the six-pattern first banner remains in the Loom input, Blue Dye remains in the dye input, and no output-slot click has yet been made after the swap.

steps.action: Left-click the Loom's right-hand output slot exactly once to take the currently offered result. Make no further Loom or inventory interaction after this click.
steps.success_cue: The output-slot click has been performed once after the input-banner swap, and the reproduction sequence is paused immediately afterward for observation.

stor.handoff_condition: The Loom's right-hand output slot has just been left-clicked once after the six-pattern first banner replaced the second banner in the occupied banner input slot, with Blue Dye and the centered-circle selection retained. Begin observation immediately, before performing any additional inventory, Loom, placement, or pattern actions.
uncertainties: The report does not specify game mode, world seed, server type, banner color, dye colors, or exact pattern designs. Creative-mode single player, White Banners, six simple red stripe patterns, and a blue centered-circle pattern are practical deterministic choices that preserve the reported Loom interaction.

The report's instruction to 'swap in the first banner' is interpreted as picking up the six-pattern banner and left-clicking the occupied Loom banner input slot so the two banners exchange positions in one inventory click.

The report explicitly requires leaving the second banner in the right side of the GUI before swapping the input banner, but it does not explicitly state the final click used to collect the result. The final output-slot click is included as a practical execution step to complete the Loom transaction before observation.

External verification was limited to the general Java Edition Loom slot roles and the use of a banner plus dye to select ordinary patterns; the Mojira report remains the source of truth for the timing-sensitive swap procedure.

source_meta._title: Acacia hanging signs cannot be crafted

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 22w42a in an unmodded single-player Creative-mode world with cheats enabled and the built-in Update 1.20 experimental data pack enabled during world creation. Use the standard crafting-table interface. The instructions assume default keyboard and mouse controls and English item names.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact Java Edition snapshot 22w42a, not the fixed snapshot 22w43a or a later version.
Create a new disposable world; the Update 1.20 experimental features must be enabled during world creation and cannot be added to an already-created 22w42a world.
Do not load additional data packs, mods, or server plugins that replace recipes.
Use Creative mode for deterministic item acquisition. This is an execution choice; the report does not require a particular game mode.
Have at least one Crafting Table, two Chains, and six Stripped Acacia Logs available before beginning the manual crafting attempt.

steps.action: Start Minecraft: Java Edition using the launcher installation configured for snapshot 22w42a. At the title screen, verify that the displayed version is 22w42a before proceeding.
steps.success_cue: The title screen identifies the running version as Minecraft Java Edition 22w42a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, and set Allow Cheats to ON. The single-player Creative configuration is used only to obtain the required items reliably.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Allow Cheats: ON
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows Creative mode and cheats enabled.

steps.action: While still creating the new world, open the Data Packs screen. Find the built-in Update 1.20 experimental pack, which may be displayed as “Update 1.20” or by its internal-style name “update_1_20”, and move it from Available to Selected using its arrow button. Select Done afterward.
steps.exact_input: Create New World -> Data Packs -> enable Update 1.20/update_1_20 -> Done
steps.success_cue: The Update 1.20 experimental data pack is in the selected/enabled data-pack list.

steps.action: If an experimental-feature warning appears, accept the warning and continue. Select Create New World.
steps.exact_input: Proceed, if prompted -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The new world begins loading with the experimental pack enabled.

steps.action: Wait until the player is in the world, surrounding terrain has rendered, and movement responds normally. Do not begin the crafting test while the world is still loading.
steps.success_cue: The player can move normally in the loaded Creative world.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the inventory control, whose default key is E, and select the Search Items tab.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory is open and a text search field is available.

steps.action: Click the search field and enter “Acacia Hanging Sign” to verify that the Update 1.20 experimental content is active. Do not take the hanging sign item; this search is only a setup check.
steps.success_cue: An Acacia Hanging Sign item appears among the Creative search results, confirming that the experimental content is enabled.

steps.action: Replace the search text with “Crafting Table”. Left-click the Crafting Table item in the results to pick up a stack, then left-click an empty hotbar slot—the hotbar is the nine-slot row at the bottom of the screen—to place it there.
steps.success_cue: A Crafting Table is present in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Replace the search text with “Chain”. Pick up the Chain item and place its stack into a different hotbar or player-inventory slot. At least two Chains are required.
steps.success_cue: The player inventory contains at least two Chains.

steps.action: Replace the search text with “Stripped Acacia Log”. Pick up the Stripped Acacia Log item and place its stack into another hotbar or player-inventory slot. At least six logs are required. Do not substitute Acacia Logs, Acacia Wood, Stripped Acacia Wood, planks, or another tree species.
steps.success_cue: The player inventory contains at least six items named Stripped Acacia Log.

steps.action: Close the inventory with E. Select the hotbar slot containing the Crafting Table using the corresponding number key or the mouse wheel. Aim at a clear ground block within reach and use the selected table with right-click to place it.
steps.exact_input: E; select the Crafting Table hotbar slot; right-click a clear ground block
steps.success_cue: A Crafting Table block is placed in the world within the player's reach.

steps.action: Optional diagnostic from the report: press T to open in-game chat, enter the report's command exactly as written with the leading slash, and press Enter. Cheats must be enabled for this command.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback indicates that recipes were granted to the player or players. If this optional diagnostic is skipped, continue to the next step.

steps.action: Aim at the placed Crafting Table and right-click it to open the 3-by-3 crafting interface.
steps.success_cue: The Crafting Table interface is open, showing a 3-by-3 input grid and an output slot.

steps.action: Optional diagnostic, only if step 12 was performed: click the recipe-book button in the Crafting Table interface, select its search field, and type “Hanging Sign”. Locate the Acacia Hanging Sign entry. Do not rely on recipe auto-fill for the primary reproduction and do not take anything from the output slot.
steps.exact_input: Click Recipe Book -> click search field -> type Hanging Sign
steps.success_cue: The recipe-book search is filtered to hanging-sign recipes and the Acacia Hanging Sign entry can be located. The crafting interface remains open.

steps.action: Prepare for the manual crafting attempt. Close the recipe-book panel if it obstructs the grid. Remove any items or ghost-filled ingredients from the 3-by-3 crafting input grid so that all nine input cells are visibly empty before manually arranging the ingredients.
steps.exact_input: Click the Recipe Book button if necessary; clear all nine crafting-grid cells
steps.success_cue: All nine input cells in the Crafting Table grid are empty, and the Chain and Stripped Acacia Log stacks remain accessible in the player inventory.

steps.action: Place one Chain in the top-left crafting-grid cell and one Chain in the top-right cell, leaving the top-center cell empty. To place single items from a stack, left-click the Chain stack to hold it on the cursor, right-click each required grid cell once, and return the remaining stack to its inventory slot.
steps.exact_input: Chain layout: top-left = 1 Chain; top-center = empty; top-right = 1 Chain
steps.success_cue: The top crafting row contains Chain, empty cell, Chain in that order, with exactly one Chain in each occupied cell.

steps.action: Place one Stripped Acacia Log into each of the three cells in the middle row. Then place one Stripped Acacia Log in the bottom-left cell and one in the bottom-center cell. Deliberately leave the bottom-right cell empty so that the final placement can be isolated as the trigger action.
steps.exact_input: Middle row: Stripped Acacia Log, Stripped Acacia Log, Stripped Acacia Log; bottom row: Stripped Acacia Log, Stripped Acacia Log, empty
steps.success_cue: The grid contains two Chains in the top corners and five Stripped Acacia Logs across the full middle row and the first two cells of the bottom row; only the bottom-right intended ingredient cell remains empty.

steps.action: Trigger the reproduction by placing exactly one Stripped Acacia Log into the bottom-right crafting-grid cell. Do not remove ingredients, substitute oak logs, click a recipe-book entry, or interact with the output slot after this placement. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately.
steps.exact_input: right-click the bottom-right crafting-grid cell once while holding Stripped Acacia Log
steps.success_cue: The intended hanging-sign pattern is complete: Chains occupy the two top corners, the top-center cell is empty, and all six cells in the middle and bottom rows contain one Stripped Acacia Log each. No output-slot interaction has occurred.

stor.handoff_condition: The sixth Stripped Acacia Log has just been placed in the bottom-right cell, completing the intended two-Chain and six-Stripped-Acacia-Log recipe pattern in the 22w42a Crafting Table. The crafting interface is still open and the output slot has not been clicked; begin observation now.
uncertainties: The report does not specify single-player versus multiplayer, game mode, seed, coordinates, or difficulty. An unmodded single-player Creative world is selected as the simplest deterministic environment because none of those omitted conditions appears necessary for the crafting action.

The report does not explicitly mention enabling experimental features. External version documentation confirms that hanging signs in 22w42a require the Update 1.20 built-in experimental data pack to be enabled while creating the world.
The exact visible label of the built-in pack may differ by language or UI presentation; it is referred to as the Update 1.20 experimental pack and is associated with the internal name update_1_20.
The /recipe command and recipe-book search are explicitly optional in the report. They are preserved as an optional diagnostic, while the manual ingredient placement is used as the primary trigger.

The report supplies the ingredient types and quantities but not the cell-by-cell layout. The layout with Chains in the top corners and six matching stripped logs filling the bottom two rows was externally verified.

source_meta.issue links: Duplicate:inward:MC-269823:Stonecutter Items Incorrect with Custom Components
source_meta._title: Stonecutter does not support multiple recipes with the same result item type

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 24w10a in an unmodified single-player client. Use a newly created Creative-mode world with only the attached test_datapack.zip enabled. Default keyboard and mouse controls are assumed.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher is installed and can launch the exact Java Edition snapshot 24w10a.
The attachment test_datapack.zip from MC-269161 has been downloaded and is available as an intact ZIP file. Do not extract or modify it unless Minecraft rejects the ZIP itself.
Use a vanilla installation without mods. Do not enable other datapacks that add or modify stonecutting recipes.
Create a disposable test world; the report does not specify a seed, world type, difficulty, or game mode.
Creative mode is used only as a practical way to obtain a Stonecutter and Oak Planks without unrelated crafting or exploration.

steps.action: Launch the exact affected snapshot. In the Minecraft Launcher, select or create a Java Edition installation whose version is snapshot 24w10a, then start the game.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and identifies the running version as 24w10a.

steps.action: Open the single-player world list and begin creating a new world by selecting Singleplayer, then Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Set the new world's game mode to Creative. Leave the seed, world type, difficulty, and other world-generation settings at their defaults.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows Creative as the selected game mode.

steps.action: Navigate to the new world's datapack configuration screen. In the 24w10a world-creation interface, open the More tab and select Data Packs.
steps.success_cue: The Data Packs screen is open and shows sections for available and selected datapacks.

steps.action: Select Open Pack Folder. In the operating-system folder that opens, copy test_datapack.zip into that folder without changing its filename. Return to Minecraft after the copy finishes.
steps.success_cue: test_datapack.zip appears as an available datapack in the Minecraft Data Packs screen; refreshing or reopening the screen is acceptable if it does not appear immediately.

steps.action: Enable test_datapack.zip by selecting its arrow or otherwise moving it from Available to Selected. Do not enable any unrelated datapacks.
steps.success_cue: test_datapack.zip is listed in the Selected datapacks column.

steps.action: Select Done to return to world creation. If Minecraft displays a datapack validation or confirmation screen, accept only if it allows the attached pack to remain enabled.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen is visible again and no message says that test_datapack.zip failed to load.

steps.action: Create the world by selecting Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The player enters the newly generated world.

steps.action: Do not interact until initial world loading is complete. Wait for nearby terrain to render and verify that looking and moving respond normally.
steps.success_cue: Nearby ground is rendered, the loading overlay is gone, and player movement is responsive.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Open the Search Items tab, search for a Stonecutter, and place one Stonecutter into an empty hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine slots at the bottom of the inventory.
steps.success_cue: A Stonecutter is present in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: While the Creative inventory remains open, search for Oak Planks and place a stack into another empty hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: Oak Planks are present in a hotbar slot separate from the Stonecutter.

steps.action: Close the inventory with E or Esc. Select the hotbar slot containing the Stonecutter, aim at the top surface of a nearby solid ground block, and right-click to place it.
steps.exact_input: Select Stonecutter hotbar slot; right-click ground
steps.success_cue: A Stonecutter block is placed in the world within interaction range.

steps.action: Aim at the placed Stonecutter and right-click it to open its interface.
steps.success_cue: The Stonecutter interface is open, showing an input slot, a recipe-selection area, and a result slot.

steps.action: Move exactly one Oak Planks item into the Stonecutter input slot. To do this from a stack, left-click the Oak Planks stack to pick it up, right-click the Stonecutter input slot once to deposit one item, then return the remaining stack to its original inventory slot with left-click.
steps.success_cue: The Stonecutter input slot contains exactly one Oak Planks item.

steps.action: Wait for the recipe-selection area to populate. Do not remove the Oak Planks or close the interface. Confirm that the datapack has supplied the set of 16 Stonecutter recipe buttons described by the report; use the recipe-area scrollbar if necessary only to count or expose additional entries.
steps.success_cue: Sixteen selectable datapack recipe entries are available for the Oak Planks input. If the entries do not appear, stop because the attached datapack is not active.

steps.action: Click the first visible datapack recipe button in the recipe grid once. Do not take the item from the result slot.
steps.success_cue: The first clicked recipe button is selected and the Stonecutter result slot contains a Light block item; the input Oak Planks remains in place.

steps.action: Click a different recipe button once—preferably the next visible button in grid order or a button displaying a different light-level icon—and then immediately stop interacting. Do not click the result slot, shift-click the result, remove the Oak Planks, or close the interface.
steps.exact_input: Left-click a second, different recipe button once
steps.success_cue: The second recipe button is now selected, the result slot is populated, and no output item has been taken.

stor.handoff_condition: The Stonecutter remains open with one Oak Planks item in its input slot, the datapack's second distinct recipe button has just been clicked, and the resulting Light block item remains untouched in the result slot. Begin observation before any further click or inventory action.
uncertainties: The raw report names the required attachment but does not provide the contents of test_datapack.zip, so this plan assumes the original attachment is intact and compatible with snapshot 24w10a.

The report does not identify one specific recipe button or light level that is guaranteed to demonstrate the issue. It instructs the tester to click among the various datapack recipes, so the plan uses two distinct buttons and hands off immediately after the second selection.
Creative mode and a newly created single-player world are practical execution choices; the report does not specify a required game mode, seed, world type, or dedicated-server environment.
The world-creation menu wording may vary slightly within the snapshot interface, but the datapack must be enabled for the world before testing.

source_meta._title: Transmute recipes allow air as output

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 24w38a in a clean singleplayer world. Use Creative mode with commands enabled as a practical deterministic setup. Enable the attached transmute_pack.zip data pack during world creation.
preconditions: Install and launch Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 24w38a, not the listed fix version 1.21.2 Pre-Release 2 or any later version.
Obtain the report attachment named transmute_pack.zip and keep it available as a ZIP file.
Use a clean test world to avoid recipes or data packs from unrelated sources.
Use the default controls described below, or the corresponding rebound controls.
The player must have permission to execute /recipe; creating the test world in Creative mode provides commands in a singleplayer world.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation for snapshot 24w38a and start the game. Confirm the lower-left corner or title screen identifies the running version as 24w38a before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is open and displays version 24w38a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then choose Create New World. Set the game mode to Creative so that commands can be executed and a crafting table can be obtained without unrelated resource gathering.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen shows Creative as the selected game mode.

steps.action: Before creating the world, open the data-pack configuration screen using the More tab and then Data Packs. Select Open Pack Folder to open the operating-system folder into which world-creation data packs can be placed.
steps.exact_input: More -> Data Packs -> Open Pack Folder
steps.success_cue: The operating system displays the data-pack folder associated with the world being created.

steps.action: Copy the attached transmute_pack.zip file into the opened data-pack folder. Do not rename it, edit its recipe files, or extract it unless the game cannot recognize the supplied ZIP as a pack.
steps.success_cue: transmute_pack.zip is present directly inside the opened data-pack folder.

steps.action: Return to Minecraft. In the Data Packs screen, locate the newly detected pack in the Available list and activate it so that it moves to the Selected list. Confirm any prompt required to enable the pack, then select Done.
steps.success_cue: The attached pack is shown in the Selected data-packs list and Minecraft has returned to the world-creation screen.

steps.action: Create the world. If Minecraft displays a warning associated with loading a snapshot or experimental data, acknowledge it without changing or removing the attached pack.
steps.success_cue: The player enters the newly created world.

steps.action: Wait before issuing commands. Continue only after nearby terrain has rendered, the player can look and move normally, and the world is no longer showing a loading screen.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the loaded world and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Obtain a crafting table deterministically. Press T to open in-game chat, enter the exact command below with its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A crafting table is present in the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Place the crafting table into the hotbar if it is not already there. Press E to open the inventory, move the crafting table to one of the nine slots along the bottom, close the inventory with E or Esc, and select that slot using its number key or the mouse wheel.
steps.exact_input: E -> move Crafting Table to hotbar -> E or Esc -> select its hotbar slot
steps.success_cue: The crafting table is visible in the selected hotbar slot and is shown in the player's hand.

steps.action: Aim at a solid, unobstructed block within reach and use the selected crafting table on that block with right-click.
steps.success_cue: A crafting table block is placed in the world within the player's interaction range.

steps.action: Right-click the placed crafting table to open its crafting interface.
steps.success_cue: The crafting-table interface is open and shows a 3-by-3 crafting grid.

steps.action: Prepare the interface so that the recipe book will be visible during the final opening. If the recipe-book pane is collapsed, click the green book button beside the crafting grid once. If the pane is already visible, leave it open.
steps.exact_input: left-click the green Recipe Book button if the recipe-book pane is collapsed
steps.success_cue: The recipe-book pane is visibly expanded beside the 3-by-3 crafting grid.

steps.action: Close the crafting-table interface with Esc while leaving the placed crafting table where it is. Do not move far enough away to lose interaction range.
steps.success_cue: Normal world view is restored, and the same crafting table remains directly within reach.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Enter the report's command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter. Execute it only once and preserve any resulting chat feedback for the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: The command has been submitted once, chat has closed, and the player has returned to normal world control; no second attempt has been made.

steps.action: Immediately aim at the previously placed crafting table and right-click it once to open the crafting-table interface. Do not place ingredients into the grid, select another recipe, run another command, or repeatedly reopen the table.
steps.success_cue: The crafting-table interface has just opened, with the recipe-book pane expanded beside the 3-by-3 crafting grid.

stor.handoff_condition: The command /recipe give @s test:test_recipe has been executed exactly once, and the crafting-table interface has just been opened with its recipe-book pane expanded. Hand control to the observation subsystem now, before clicking recipes, placing ingredients, closing the interface, or repeating the command.
uncertainties: The contents of transmute_pack.zip were not included in the supplied report text, so this plan assumes the attachment is a directly loadable data-pack ZIP containing the recipe identified as test:test_recipe.

The report does not specify a game mode. Creative mode with commands enabled is selected only as a practical deterministic way to satisfy command permissions and obtain a crafting table; it is not asserted to be a bug requirement.
The pack's displayed title in the Data Packs screen may differ from the attachment filename transmute_pack.zip. Identify it by adding only that attachment to the clean world's data-pack folder.

The plan assumes the expanded/collapsed recipe-book state remains selected after closing and reopening the crafting table. If the pane is unexpectedly collapsed at the final opening, expand it once without performing any other crafting action, then hand off immediately.

source_meta._title: Resin bricks cannot be placed or used inside smithing tables

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 24w45a in a new vanilla single-player Creative-mode world. No particular seed, coordinates, difficulty, structure, multiplayer server, resource pack, or data pack is required by the report. Instructions assume the English (US) interface and default mouse/keyboard controls.
preconditions: Enable historical snapshots in the Minecraft Launcher and install an installation that launches exactly Java Edition snapshot 24w45a.
Do not perform this reproduction in fix version 24w46a; the affected version specified by the report is 24w45a.
Use an unmodified vanilla client unless comparison against a modified environment is separately required.

The official 24w45a notes identify Resin Brick, rather than Resin Clump, as the intended armor-trim material. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/da-dk/article/minecraft-snapshot-24w45a?utm_source=openai))
Creative mode is used only as a deterministic way to obtain the report's required items without exploration, crafting, or commands.
The smithing workflow requires an armor piece, an armor-trim smithing template, and a trim material. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/smithing-table?utm_source=openai))

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation configured for Java Edition snapshot 24w45a and start the game. On the title screen, verify the displayed version before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft Java Edition title screen is open and its version text identifies the running game as 24w45a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, and create the world. Leave the seed and other world-generation settings at their defaults because the report supplies no required seed or location.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player has entered a new 24w45a world in Creative mode.

steps.action: Do not begin item setup until the immediate terrain has rendered and normal player movement and inventory input respond without initial world-loading delay.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is visible, the player can move normally, and pressing E opens the inventory without a loading delay.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Open the Search Items tab, click its search field, enter the exact item name "Smithing Table", and move one Smithing Table result into hotbar slot 1. The hotbar is the row of nine quick-access slots along the bottom of the inventory.
steps.success_cue: One Smithing Table is present in hotbar slot 1.

steps.action: In the Creative inventory's Search Items tab, replace the existing search text with "Sentry Armor Trim Smithing Template" and move one matching template into hotbar slot 2. This is the deterministic example used for the report's instruction to obtain any armor trim.
steps.success_cue: One Sentry Armor Trim Smithing Template is present in hotbar slot 2.

steps.action: Replace the search text with "Iron Chestplate" and move one ordinary, untrimmed Iron Chestplate into hotbar slot 3. This is the deterministic example used for the report's instruction to obtain any chestplate.
steps.success_cue: One untrimmed Iron Chestplate is present in hotbar slot 3.

steps.action: Replace the search text with "Resin Brick" and move one Resin Brick item into hotbar slot 4. Select the singular Resin Brick item, not a Resin Clump and not a Resin Bricks building block.
steps.success_cue: One Resin Brick item is present in hotbar slot 4 alongside the smithing table, template, and chestplate.

steps.action: Press E to close the Creative inventory. Verify that hotbar slots 1 through 4 contain, in order, the Smithing Table, Sentry Armor Trim Smithing Template, Iron Chestplate, and Resin Brick.
steps.success_cue: The inventory is closed and all four required items are visible in the hotbar.

steps.action: Select hotbar slot 1 so that the Smithing Table is the active held item. Aim at the top face of a nearby solid ground block and use the place/use action, which is right-click by default, to place the Smithing Table.
steps.exact_input: Hotbar slot 1; right-click a solid ground block
steps.success_cue: A Smithing Table block is placed within interaction range of the player.

steps.action: Aim at the placed Smithing Table and right-click it once to open its interface.
steps.success_cue: The Smithing Table interface is open, showing three input slots to the left of an arrow and an output slot to the right.

steps.action: In the inventory section at the bottom of the Smithing Table interface, left-click and drag the Sentry Armor Trim Smithing Template from hotbar slot 2 into the leftmost of the three input slots, then release the mouse button.
steps.exact_input: Left-click-drag Sentry Armor Trim Smithing Template -> leftmost template input slot
steps.success_cue: The Sentry Armor Trim Smithing Template visibly occupies the leftmost input slot.

steps.action: Left-click and drag the untrimmed Iron Chestplate from hotbar slot 3 into the middle input slot, then release the mouse button. Do not click the output slot.
steps.exact_input: Left-click-drag Iron Chestplate -> middle equipment input slot
steps.success_cue: The template remains in the left input slot and the Iron Chestplate visibly occupies the middle input slot.

steps.action: With the Smithing Table interface still open, left-click and drag the Resin Brick from hotbar slot 4 onto the rightmost input slot—the material/addition slot immediately to the left of the arrow—and release the mouse button exactly once. Make no further inventory clicks after this placement attempt.
steps.exact_input: Left-click-drag Resin Brick -> rightmost material/addition input slot; release once
steps.success_cue: The Resin Brick placement attempt has just been completed while the Smithing Table interface remains open for immediate inspection.

stor.handoff_condition: The Sentry Armor Trim Smithing Template and Iron Chestplate have been loaded into their smithing input slots, and the Resin Brick has just been released once onto the rightmost material/addition input slot. Begin observation immediately before making any further click, moving items, closing the interface, or repeating the attempt.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode or item-acquisition method. Creative mode and the Creative inventory are used as a deterministic setup choice, not as a claimed requirement of the bug.

The report permits any armor trim and any chestplate but does not name particular examples. This plan uses a Sentry Armor Trim Smithing Template and an untrimmed Iron Chestplate; these selections are practical examples rather than report-mandated items.
The phrase "any armor trim" is interpreted as any Armor Trim Smithing Template, because a template is the item placed into the Smithing Table to select a trim pattern.
The report does not state whether the test must be single-player or multiplayer. A single-player world is selected because no server-specific condition is described.
The report does not specify a seed, coordinates, difficulty, or world-generation settings, so no deterministic location beyond a newly created world is required.
